audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher genealogies, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for military census language, wives and fertility, variant Benjamin lists, Bilhah, Zelophehad's daughters, women as named builders and sisters, cattle-raiding deaths, mourning, and geographic claims.

verses.restored: Sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron—four.
Sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel, heads of ancestral houses of Tola, mighty warriors in generations; their number in days of David was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
Son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. Sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah—five including their father, all leaders.
With them by generations and ancestral houses were thirty-six thousand troops for war, because they had many wives and sons.
Their brothers among all families of Issachar, mighty warriors enrolled by genealogy, were eighty-seven thousand.
Sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael—three in this list.
Sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri—five heads of ancestral houses, mighty warriors; enrolled number was twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
Sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were sons of Becher.
Their enrollment by generations and ancestral heads, mighty warriors, was twenty thousand two hundred.
Son of Jediael: Bilhan. Sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these sons of Jediael, by ancestral heads, were seventeen thousand two hundred warriors able to go out for battle.
Shuppim and Huppim were descendants of Ir; Hushim was descendant/son of Aher, according to difficult text.
Sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, descendants of Bilhah.
Descendants of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his Aramean concubine bore; she also bore Machir father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife connected with Huppim and Shuppim; name of his sister/wife was Maacah. Name of second was Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.
Maacah wife of Machir bore a son and called his name Peresh; name of his brother was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
Son of Ulam: Bedan. These were descendants of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
Sons of Shemida: Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
Descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead, whom men of Gath born in land killed because they came down to take their livestock.
Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He went to his wife; she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Beriah, because calamity had come upon his house.
His daughter was Sheerah, who built lower and upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sheerah.
Rephah was his son, Resheph, Telah his son, Tahan his son,
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, Joshua his son.
Their possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns, eastward Naaran, westward Gezer and its towns, Shechem and its towns as far as Ayyah/Gaza and its towns.
Along borders of Manasseh: Beth-shean and towns, Taanach and towns, Megiddo and towns, Dor and towns. In these lived descendants of Joseph son of Israel.
Sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister.
Sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, father of Birzaith.
Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua their sister.
Sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were children of Japhlet.
Sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
Sons of his brother Helem: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
Sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
Sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these were descendants of Asher, heads of ancestral houses, chosen mighty warriors, chiefs among leaders. Their enrolled number for war and battle was twenty-six thousand.

translation_notes: Large military counts reflect the Chronicler's administrative and martial interests and may not define communal worth.
Verse 4 links troop growth with many wives and sons; women are not reproductive infrastructure, and family size is not a Divine score.
Benjamin's genealogy differs substantially from Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles 8; textual and compositional audit is required.
Bilhah is remembered as ancestral mother of Naphtali's line; her enslaved/secondary-wife status in Genesis must not be erased.
Zelophehad's daughters carry an important legal tradition about women's inheritance that the brief mention should not obscure.
Ezer and Elead die during an attempted livestock seizure. Their deaths are grieved, but cattle raiding is not morally innocent.
Ephraim's prolonged mourning and communal comfort validate grief rather than demanding rapid spiritual recovery.
Sheerah is explicitly remembered as a builder of towns; women's engineering and civic leadership must not be minimized.
Territorial and town lists are ancient identity maps, not modern deeds.
safety_note: Reject militarism, fertility hierarchy, polygyny apologetics, cattle-raiding romanticism, gender erasure, and modern territorial claims. Center Bilhah, Maacah, Zelophehad's daughters, Hammolecheth, Serah, Shua, Sheerah the builder, and Ephraim's unshamed grief.
